newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka cement output to rise over 70 pct-paper.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka cement output to rise over 70 pct-paper.

text.p: Sri Lankan cement companies plan to boost production by more than 70 percent over the next four years involving an investment of more than seven billion rupees ($119.5 million), the Daily News said on Tuesday.
The government-owned newspaper quoted an official at the Ministry of Industrial Development as saying output would rise to 2.40 million tonnes per year from 1.39 million tonnes.

The privately-owned Puttalam Cement company would raise output to 800,000 tonnes a year by the end of 2001 from 480,000 tonnes. This would involve a total investment for the company of some 4.72 billion rupees, it said.

Another local company, Ruhunu Cement Co Ltd, would increase production to 456,000 tonnes from 192,000 tonnes, while Tokyo Cement Co (Lanka) Ltd and Fuji Cement would raise capacity at their plant to 460,000 tonnes from 240,000, it said.
Tokyo Cement and Fuji Cement would spend a total of 540 million rupees on the expansion, the newspaper added.
Officials at the ministry and cement firms were unavailable for immediate comment.
The newspaper said demand for cement from the Sri Lankan building industry had increased recently, leading to higher imports.
It quoted officials as saying Sri Lanka had spent more than 34 billion rupees worth of foreign exchange importing cement over the last five years.
The country could be self-sufficient in cement if adequate investment in the industry was available, it said. ($1 = 58.6 rupees)
